answer: Each identity files a customs declaration for a walnut batch at a reef port, locks an 80-credit bond, and pays 30 filing and 100 tariff on 200 kilograms. It is weighed against a marble standard block, and ticket, seal, and key enter the reef ledger. Auditors recompute the tariff from the posted weight; under-declaration, reuse, or a marble mismatch burns the bond. The k-th fake pays 170 and locks a new 80 bond, so 1,000 fakes cost 170,000 plus 80,000 at risk. A rented-declaration ring fails: one ticket binds one seal, one reading, one key. An honest agent pays 170 once and recovers the bond.
